questions.stem: What two substances must be present for iron to rust?
questions.explanation: Both oxygen and water must be present for iron to rust. If either is absent, rusting does not occur. This is why iron does not rust in dry air or in water that has been boiled to remove dissolved oxygen.

questions.stem: What is the chemical name for rust?
questions.explanation: Rust is hydrated iron(III) oxide, which has the formula Fe₂O₃·xH₂O. It forms when iron reacts with oxygen and water over time. The 'hydrated' part means it contains water molecules.

questions.stem: Which method of rust prevention works by coating the iron with a more reactive metal?
questions.explanation: Galvanising coats iron with zinc, which is more reactive than iron. The zinc provides sacrificial protection: even if the coating is scratched, the zinc corrodes preferentially instead of the iron, because zinc is higher in the reactivity series.

options.text: It reacts with the iron to make it unreactive
It acts as a barrier, preventing oxygen and water from reaching the iron surface

questions.explanation: Painting acts as a barrier method of rust prevention. The paint layer keeps oxygen and water away from the iron surface, so the rusting reaction cannot occur. However, if the paint is scratched, the exposed iron will rust.

options.text: Covering iron with a layer of paint
Attaching a more reactive metal to iron so that it corrodes instead of the iron
Coating iron with a less reactive metal

questions.explanation: Sacrificial protection involves attaching blocks of a more reactive metal (like zinc or magnesium) to iron structures. The more reactive metal oxidises (corrodes) in preference to the iron, 'sacrificing' itself to protect the iron.

questions.stem: In an experiment to investigate rusting, an iron nail is placed in boiled water with a layer of oil on top. What is the purpose of boiling the water and adding oil?

options.text: To make the water hotter so the nail rusts faster
To remove dissolved oxygen from the water and prevent oxygen from re-entering
To add a protective coating to the nail

questions.explanation: Boiling removes dissolved oxygen from the water, and the oil layer prevents oxygen from the air from dissolving back in. This shows that without oxygen, the iron nail does not rust, proving that oxygen is needed for rusting.

questions.stem: How does corrosion differ from rusting?

options.text: Corrosion only affects iron; rusting affects all metals
Rusting specifically refers to the corrosion of iron; corrosion is a broader term for the chemical attack on any metal

questions.explanation: Corrosion is the general term for the destruction of a metal by chemical reactions with substances in the environment. Rusting is a specific type of corrosion that only applies to iron (and steel), involving reaction with oxygen and water.
